name: Consent
challenges: Revocation is hard to enforce when data has already been copied or shared. Granularity—what exactly was consented to, for how long, for what purpose—is often unclear. Demonstrating lawful basis and consent to regulators or data subjects is difficult at scale; consent is frequently buried in long terms or obtained without meaningful choice.
opportunities: Consent receipts—tamper-evident records of what was consented to, when, and by whom—can be anchored on-chain and presented to processors and auditors. Selective disclosure and ZK can support minimal data use in line with consent. Revocation or withdrawal can be recorded and verified; GDPR Art. 7 and W3C work on consent receipts align with these patterns.
